source.title: Persona Corruption and Role Miscasting in Emergent Misalignment

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full post, but some model names, equations, and plotted values are absent from the text rendering.
record.tranche_reason: It examines the proposed mechanism with persona-space measurements and steering, rather than reproducing the original training and evaluation recipe.
record.gate_note: The post reports its own measurements of persona shifts, misalignment rates, and steering outcomes. Referenced findings from other work are not recorded as results. Numeric values visible only in omitted plots cannot be recovered from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The post uses existing EM model organisms and measures their misalignment rates. It tests whether a shared persona-space direction tracks and mediates EM, by correlation and by steering against the direction while measuring misalignment rates. This is a different method on V5's question.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors claim suggestive, preliminary evidence that narrow fine-tuning produces a single global persona shift, which they read as persona corruption, and that assistant/default detachment tracks EM, which they read as role miscasting. They add that steering against the shift reduces misalignment in Qwen but not Llama. They admit the shift also occurs in aligned controls and that the two mechanisms may not be separable.
record.recipe_differences: Analyzes existing narrow-fine-tuning model organisms and non-EM controls, but focuses on persona geometry and steering rather than reproducing the original behavioral evaluation and training comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Mean versus median changes values only marginally (r ≈ 0.99); random half-casts shift excess values by roughly a tenth of the typical effect, with within-family ordering retaining its sign in 99.9% of draws. Global-shift steering reduces misalignment across Qwen but fails in Llama; default-excess steering is less successful.

fits_no_version.finding: Average per-role misalignment does not significantly track general misalignment; roles shifting most toward evil have the highest role misalignment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Role-specific misalignment under role-play prompts is decoupled from default-persona EM rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Default-axis rotation is as large in an off-topic, non-misaligned control as in EM organisms. Persona-cloud dimensionality increases in all fine-tunes, controls included.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persona-geometry changes flag generic fine-tuning drift, not misalignment specifically.

record.problems: The authors call the results preliminary and say the sample is limited: there are three to five organisms per family, making textbook p-values unreliable, and only Qwen has enough organisms for significance. Many per-model plotted values are absent from the supplied text. The authors also note that role inertia and context-dependent elicitation may compromise interpretation, and that persona corruption and role miscasting may not be geometrically separable.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for the unrelated emotion-vector exploration or speculative discussion of the ExploitGym incident. Numeric per-model values that appear only in plots are unavailable in the supplied text.

untested.parts: The study analyses existing organisms and does not compare insecure-code fine-tuning against secure or educational controls.
Organisms from other narrow datasets are used, but their EM rates are not compared against controls.
Inoculation and benign retraining are not tested. Steering is not the version's mitigation.
No model-size sweep, seeds, coherence filters or training-stage analysis. The robustness checks reported concern the geometric metric only.
Not tested whether the direction mediates EM across all fine-tune datasets, as opposed to across organisms in a family. Coherence after steering is not reported.

record.verdict_notes: V5 limits_scope, condition 'Llama family; aligned controls; non-Qwen families'. Reason: global-shift steering fails in Llama (R9) and default-excess steering works less well (R10). The shift appears in the aligned control too (R1, R3), evil-direction alignment holds only in Qwen (R11), and the EM correlation is significant only in Qwen (R4). Row ids: R1, R3, R4, R9, R10, R11. The reader's V7 labels are removed because R5 and R6 test metric robustness, not EM robustness. Small LessWrong project; most numbers sit in plots and are absent from the text. Gemma is the only full fine-tune, so family and tuning method are confounded there.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report a direct comparison of insecure-code fine-tuning against secure-code and class-requested insecure-code controls on neutral-prompt misalignment rates.
Does not test the specified other narrow fine-tuning datasets as causes of broad misalignment.
No test of narrow in-context examples alone.
The measurements do not establish that a persona feature causally mediates misalignment or that the same direction mediates it across all fine-tunes.
Steering against measured shifts is not a test of inoculation framing or brief benign retraining.
No size sweep, seed robustness test, coherence-filter analysis, or training-stage comparison. The post does report robustness checks over persona casts and mean-versus-median aggregation.
